record.paper_title: Spin-density-functional theory: some open problems and application to inhomogeneous Heisenberg models
record.original_question: What is the best theoretically consistent and computationally practical way to treat noncollinear spin configurations in spin-density-functional theory beyond the local-spin-density approximation, given that standard noncollinear SDFT implementations assume the exchange-correlation magnetic field is parallel to the spin magnetization, while generalized-gradient-type functionals can make that field nonparallel and alternatives such as staggered-density formulations require new functionals and more complicated Kohn-Sham equations?

evidence.quote: The standard spin-up spin-down formulation of SDFT is incapable of describing spin configurations that are eigenstates of the square of the total spin operator Ŝ2, but not its z− component, Ŝz.

Standard implementations of noncollinear SDFT assume parallelity between Bxc and m(r), and can thus not be used consistently with GGA-type functionals. What the best way is to treat noncollinearity beyond LSDA is an open question at present.

As an alternative to formulations in terms of the spin magnetization, it has been proposed, e.g., to employ the spin-offdiagonal element of the density matrix (the so called ’staggered density’ [20]), but this requires the construction of functionals of this new variable, and the solution of more complicated KS equations [21].

artifact.status_search_result: Considerable progress has been made since the problem was posed. Source-free xc magnetic field constructions (Sharma et al., 2018), the "signed canonical" GGA formulation with screening of unstable terms (Pittalis et al. and later Bulik–Scalmani–Frisch developments), orbital-dependent / EXX noncollinear functionals (2018), and recent reformulations (Phys. Rev. Research 5, 013036, 2023) provide consistent noncollinear GGA schemes with nonvanishing local torque, proper collinear limit, and improved numerical stability. However, no single formulation is universally accepted as optimal: each existing scheme trades off rotational invariance, treatment of longitudinal vs. transverse gradients, torque properties, and stability differently. The question of the "best" theoretically consistent and practical scheme therefore remains partially solved rather than settled.

status_evidence.title: Noncollinear density functional theory
status_evidence.snippet: New formulation of noncollinear DFT for GGA functionals ('signed canonical' theory) with screening algorithm addressing prior limitations: collinear limit, rotational invariance, and numerical instability in small-magnetization regions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work proposes a noncollinear GGA formulation addressing key consistency issues, indicating partial resolution.

status_evidence.title: Source-Free Exchange-Correlation Magnetic Fields in Density Functional Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes making B_xc source-free, expressing functionals in terms of curl of magnetization, offering an alternative consistent formulation.
status_evidence.claim: An alternative consistent treatment of noncollinearity beyond LSDA has been proposed.

status_evidence.title: Density-functional theory for systems with noncollinear spin: orbital-dependent exchange-correlation functionals
status_evidence.snippet: Develops orbital-dependent xc functionals for noncollinear SDFT applied to Hubbard dimer, addressing the failure of LSDA-based parallelity.
status_evidence.claim: Orbital-dependent functionals provide a route beyond LSDA for noncollinear spin.

status_evidence.title: A New Approach to Noncollinear Spin Density Functional Theory beyond the LDA
status_evidence.snippet: Scalmani–Frisch GGA modification giving nonvanishing magnetic torques, though with the restriction of equal treatment of longitudinal and transverse gradients.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple competing GGA noncollinear schemes exist, none universally optimal.
